title: Ethiopian Groundnut Cake
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Groundnut Cake — roasted peanuts mixed with caramelised honey and sugar, pressed into a flat slab and cut into squares. Similar to sesame brittle but using peanuts — the Ethiopian market confection.
longDesc: Ethiopian groundnut cake follows the same caramelised confection tradition as sesame brittle (ETH174) — the peanuts provide more protein and fat, producing a more substantial confection.
ingredients: 1.5 cups raw peanuts — roasted and roughly chopped
steps: In a heavy pan: combine honey, sugar, and salt.
Cook over medium heat until golden and reaches hard crack (150°C).
Remove from heat. Add peanuts. Stir quickly.
Pour immediately onto lined sheet. Spread thin.
chefTips: See ETH174 for the caramel technique — identical process.
Add mitmita to the peanuts for a spiced version.
commonMistakes: Not reaching hard crack — sticky brittle.
culturalNote: Ethiopian groundnut cake is the affordable luxury of the market — a piece of sweet, crunchy peanut caramel from a street vendor is a small joy available to every Ethiopian.
